title: Lawmakers raise alarm at Google plan to acquire Spirit Airlines data for AI models
source_used: The Record from Recorded Future News (read in full); Reuters page returned HTTP 401, and a short Economic Times summary of the Reuters story was seen
key_facts: On Thursday (8 Oct 2026) more than 100 members of Congress (the letter has 114 signers) wrote to the chief executives of Google and Spirit Airlines asking them to halt a deal.
Google would get Spirit's internal data in exchange for $10 million paid to the failed carrier; Google wants it to train AI models.
Rep. Steven Horsford said the data would include about 100 million emails, 500 million Microsoft Teams messages, employment contracts, timecard records and payroll and tax information.
The letter, led by Horsford and Sen. Elizabeth Warren, says removing names and email addresses does not necessarily make a dataset anonymous in the context of modern AI.
Google says it is not looking to buy personal information; the data will be excluded or de-identified by an independent third party before Google receives it.
Spirit is defunct; almost 1,000 people in Las Vegas lost jobs after it announced in May it would shut down.
quote_evidence: Google wants the data to train AI models and has said it will be deidentified.
Removing names, email addresses, or other direct identifiers does not necessarily make a dataset anonymous,
The information will either be completely excluded or will be deidentified by an independent third party before Google receives any data.
why_it_matters_hint: Former airline employees' private messages and records could end up in AI training data, and lawmakers doubt that standard de-identification protects them.
notes: Reuters (401) not readable; an Economic Times summary of the Reuters story says 'more than 120' lawmakers, while The Record counts 114 signers and says 'more than 100'. The entry uses The Record's figures.
